holidays.name: National Cheese Pizza Day
holidays.description: A day for pizza purists who want nothing but dough, sauce, and gooey melted cheese. No pepperoni, no pineapple, no drama. Just the classic slice that has united birthday parties and late-night cravings for generations.
holidays.origin: Like many American food holidays, it grew out of food-industry promotion and social media enthusiasm rather than an official proclamation. It sits on September 5 in many unofficial holiday calendars.
holidays.funFact: The modern pizza Margherita, a simple cheese-and-tomato pie, is famously said to have been created in Naples in 1889 to honor Queen Margherita of Savoy, with toppings that echoed the colors of the Italian flag.

holidays.name: International Day of Charity
holidays.description: A day set aside to celebrate generosity, kindness, and helping others, whether by donating, volunteering, or simply lending a hand to a neighbor. It is a rare holiday where the weirdest thing you can do is be unexpectedly nice.
holidays.origin: The United Nations General Assembly designated September 5 as the International Day of Charity in 2012. The date marks the anniversary of the death of Mother Teresa in 1997.
holidays.funFact: Mother Teresa won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1979 and was canonized as Saint Teresa of Calcutta in 2016, almost 19 years after her death.

holidays.name: Be Late for Something Day
holidays.description: A tongue-in-cheek holiday that encourages you to show up fashionably late, just once, with zero guilt. Perfect for chronic early birds who need a break from their own punctuality.
holidays.origin: This unofficial observance appears in quirky holiday calendars as a playful counterbalance to the pressure to always be on time. It is typically listed on September 5 and has no single known founder.
holidays.funFact: The phrase 'fashionably late' is often tied to social etiquette in which arriving 15 to 30 minutes after a party start time is considered polite, since it gives hosts time to finish preparing.

holidays.name: Teachers' Day in India
holidays.description: A day when students across India thank their teachers with cards, flowers, songs, and sometimes role-reversal events where students teach the class for the day. Expect a lot of nervous 15-year-olds in sarees and blazers pretending to be their math teacher.
holidays.origin: It honors the birthday of Dr. Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan, a philosopher, scholar, and second President of India, born September 5, 1888. When friends suggested celebrating his birthday, he reportedly asked that it be observed as Teachers' Day instead.
holidays.funFact: Radhakrishnan was nominated for the Nobel Prize in Literature multiple times and also nominated for the Nobel Peace Prize, though he never won.

holidays.name: National Brazilian Day Celebration of Amazon Day
holidays.description: Brazil marks Amazon Day to celebrate the world's largest rainforest and the rivers, wildlife, and communities that make it one of Earth's most vital ecosystems. It is a day for rainforest awareness, with a lot of love for jaguars, river dolphins, and giant water lilies.
holidays.origin: Brazil established Dia da Amazônia on September 5 in 2007 to commemorate the creation of the Province of the Amazon in 1850 and to raise awareness of conservation.
holidays.funFact: The Amazon rainforest is home to the pink river dolphin, or boto, which is the subject of Brazilian folklore claiming it can turn into a charming man at night.
